advisory.summary: PHP uses longjmp() for OOM. In some contexts request memory is temporarily reachable before it is fully initialised; an allocation failure there leaves request memory invalid. Request shutdown may then read or branch on it. Multiple multipart OOM strategies reach this state. Confirmed RCE on Apache mod_php; FPM is supported as susceptible by source analysis but no complete FPM exploit was demonstrated for the startup path (FPM exits the child on startup failure).
advisory.title: RCE via OOM corruption

alternative_explanations: Application/extension allocation failure unrelated to the advisory.
Generic PHP fatal error or resource exhaustion unrelated to CVE-2026-109618.
PHP banner spoofed/stripped, or a distro backport changed the effective build.
Higher memory_limit or a different SAPI prevented the advisory path.

patch_evidence.details: CVE-2026-109618: PHP 8.2.12 is below fixed release 8.2.35.; CVE-2026-109619: PHP 8.2.12 is below fixed release 8.2.35.

proof_limitations: No negative result proves absence of the vulnerability.
An HTTP 500/502/503/504, timeout, empty body or connection reset is not evidence of OOM or of CVE-2026-109618.
A PHP OOM proves only that an allocation failed; it does not prove the invalid-state shutdown path.
OOM observed in application code has a different root cause from the advisory's startup/parser path.
A worker crash is a worker failure, not automatically this CVE.
EXPOSED_BUILD is an exposure assessment; no CVE path was exercised.
remediation: Upgrade to PHP 8.2.35 / 8.3.36 / 8.4.27 / 8.5.12 or later (the only complete mitigation).

If upgrading is impossible, administratively set memory_limit=-1 and restart every worker; this removes the predictable control point but is not complete (mmap/underlying allocation failure can still longjmp).
Keep post_max_size conservative and enforce the decoded request size independently at the frontend.
Bound multipart parts, headers per part, input nesting and uploads; reject multipart bodies entirely if the application does not use them.
Do not use RLIMIT_AS/RLIMIT_DATA as a mitigation: they make mmap fail and can re-enter the vulnerable longjmp path.
Disabling session.upload_progress is NOT a mitigation for 109618.

advisory.summary: Worker-persistent global state can point at request-owned memory. If a producer request publishes such state and is interrupted (fatal/OOM) before its matching reset, a consumer operation in a later request handled by the same worker may use the stale state. Confirmed consumers include pre-initialisation INI diagnostics and session upload progress. Producer and consumer must hit the same worker; request/worker correlation is mandatory evidence.
advisory.title: RCE via stale global state

alternative_explanations: Producer and consumer were handled by different workers.
The consumer performed normal initialisation rather than reading stale state.
The producer OOM/fatal did not publish request-owned global state.
A worker was recycled between requests (same PID may be a new process).
Application/session logic produced the diagnostic independently of stale state.
A reflected marker or static response was mistaken for a canary effect.

proof_limitations: HTTP keep-alive does not identify a PHP-FPM worker; same-worker proof needs a worker PID or equivalent telemetry.
A single OOM is not proof of stale global state.
A consumer reading state is not proof that the state belonged to a freed request.
An HTTP 500/502/503/504, timeout or empty body is not producer/consumer evidence.
No negative result proves absence of the vulnerability.
findings.proof_method: telemetry: state_publish + same worker PID + producer end before consumer + consumer early operation
remediation: Upgrade to PHP 8.2.35 / 8.3.36 / 8.4.27 / 8.5.12 or later (the only reliable mitigation; there is no complete generic config fix).
PHP 8.5 only: set fatal_error_backtraces=0 administratively and restart every worker to remove the confirmed backtrace producer.
Session lifecycle path only: set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 administratively and restart every worker. This does not cover other state families.
Remove attacker-reachable fatal errors (including request timeouts) and diagnostics emitted before request initialisation or during cleanup.
Prefer startup php.ini / FPM pool configuration over per-request INI overrides; remove obsolete or invalid directives.
Consider pm.max_requests=1 to shorten worker state lifetime.
